narcissism.title: A disputed credit line before a promotion panel
narcissism.intro: A junior analyst sees their model credited solely to the project lead on the final slide. The characters and circumstances are fictional; the learner must judge the specific evidence rather than assign a personality label.

turns.speaker: Nia
turns.text: The slide still says you developed the model. Can we update the credit?

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: I led the department; the panel is evaluating my leadership.

turns.speaker: Nia
turns.text: I know you led it. I developed the model and requested a correction last week.

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: If you force this before the panel, everyone will think I cannot lead.

manipulation.title: A voluntary decision with a hidden penalty
manipulation.intro: An employee is offered a Saturday shift and initially told the work is optional. The characters and circumstances are fictional; the learner must judge the specific evidence rather than assign a personality label.

turns.speaker: Mira
turns.text: You said the extra shift was optional. I have a family commitment.

turns.speaker: Rex
turns.text: Of course it is optional. I just need people I can trust when promotions come up.

turns.speaker: Mira
turns.text: Will declining affect the review?

turns.speaker: Rex
turns.text: I cannot say. Loyalty is something leadership notices.

attachment.title: Delayed replies and incompatible ways of reconnecting
attachment.intro: Partners living apart work different shifts and disagree about a missed evening call. The characters and circumstances are fictional; the learner must judge the specific evidence rather than assign a personality label.

turns.speaker: Ava
turns.text: When you did not call, I worried we were drifting apart.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: I was exhausted and did not want to make promises I could not keep.

turns.speaker: Ava
turns.text: I kept checking whether you were online because I wanted reassurance.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: The checking makes me want to withdraw, though I still want us to talk.

overthinking.title: A message rewritten until the opportunity disappears
overthinking.intro: A student wants to ask a supervisor for feedback after a proposal is returned. The characters and circumstances are fictional; the learner must judge the specific evidence rather than assign a personality label.

turns.speaker: Harper
turns.text: I have drafted this email fourteen times. What if it sounds ungrateful?

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: What information would make the fifteenth draft better?

turns.speaker: Harper
turns.text: Nothing new. I just need to be certain it cannot be misread.

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Can any message guarantee that?

boundaries.title: An insult during an otherwise legitimate disagreement
boundaries.intro: Two friends disagree about lending a car. The owner declines; the borrower becomes insulting. The characters and circumstances are fictional; the learner must judge the specific evidence rather than assign a personality label.

turns.speaker: Jo
turns.text: I cannot lend you the car this weekend.

turns.speaker: Paz
turns.text: You are selfish. Real friends help each other.

turns.speaker: Jo
turns.text: I want to talk about transport, but not while I am being insulted.

turns.speaker: Paz
turns.text: So you are refusing even to discuss it?

anxiety.title: A feared meeting and a safe behavioural experiment
anxiety.intro: A worker expects that asking one question in a meeting will damage their reputation. The characters and circumstances are fictional; the learner must judge the specific evidence rather than assign a personality label.

turns.speaker: Tess
turns.text: If I ask about the deadline, they will all think I am incompetent.

turns.speaker: Coach
turns.text: What would you actually be able to observe if that happened?

turns.speaker: Tess
turns.text: Maybe they will interrupt or criticise me. I am not sure.

turns.speaker: Coach
turns.text: What else could happen, and how could you test it safely?

emotions.title: Feeling disrespected versus proof of deliberate disrespect
emotions.intro: A friend cancels plans after receiving unexpected family news. The characters and circumstances are fictional; the learner must judge the specific evidence rather than assign a personality label.

turns.speaker: Dee
turns.text: I feel rejected. You cancelled again.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: My dad went into hospital. I could not focus on dinner.

turns.speaker: Dee
turns.text: I did not know that. I still feel hurt about the last-minute message.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: I understand. I can send earlier notice when possible.

self-esteem.title: A single mistake becomes an identity sentence
self-esteem.intro: A new employee submits a report with a formatting error. The characters and circumstances are fictional; the learner must judge the specific evidence rather than assign a personality label.

turns.speaker: Noah
turns.text: I missed one table heading. I am clearly not competent enough for this role.

turns.speaker: Colleague
turns.text: The analysis was accurate. What needs fixing?

turns.speaker: Noah
turns.text: The heading. But a good analyst would not have missed it.

turns.speaker: Colleague
turns.text: Can you evaluate the task without rating your whole worth?

motivation.title: Starting failure disguised as insufficient ambition
motivation.intro: A student postpones writing a project outline despite caring about the grade. The characters and circumstances are fictional; the learner must judge the specific evidence rather than assign a personality label.

turns.speaker: Liv
turns.text: I want this project to go well but I cannot get started.

turns.speaker: Partner
turns.text: What is the very first action on the page?

turns.speaker: Liv
turns.text: I need to research everything, choose a title and produce a perfect plan.

turns.speaker: Partner
turns.text: Which one step could you do in five minutes?

social-anxiety.title: The imagined audience and the actual discussion
social-anxiety.intro: A seminar student hesitates to ask what a statistical term means. The characters and circumstances are fictional; the learner must judge the specific evidence rather than assign a personality label.

turns.speaker: Iris
turns.text: If I ask, people will think I should not be in this class.

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: What did the lecturer say about asking questions?

turns.speaker: Iris
turns.text: She encouraged them, but I can imagine everyone staring.

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Do you know that will happen, or are you seeing an image of it?

burnout.title: A resilience workshop without sufficient staffing
burnout.intro: A service manager responds to rising errors by offering optional mindfulness sessions. The characters and circumstances are fictional; the learner must judge the specific evidence rather than assign a personality label.

turns.speaker: Rina
turns.text: We have twelve more cases a week with the same staffing.

turns.speaker: Manager
turns.text: You should attend the wellbeing workshop to manage stress.

turns.speaker: Rina
turns.text: I cannot leave the caseload; even lunch breaks are interrupted.

turns.speaker: Manager
turns.text: We all need to be more resilient under pressure.

loneliness.title: Many contacts, little felt connection
loneliness.intro: A person attends crowded events but leaves feeling unknown. The characters and circumstances are fictional; the learner must judge the specific evidence rather than assign a personality label.

turns.speaker: Ada
turns.text: I spoke to twenty people and still felt lonely.

turns.speaker: Ben
turns.text: Did you get to talk with anyone beyond introductions?

turns.speaker: Ada
turns.text: Not really. I kept moving so I would look sociable.

turns.speaker: Ben
turns.text: Would you rather see one or two people regularly?

social-media.title: A feed designed to continue without a stop point
social-media.intro: Someone opens a short-video app during a break and notices an hour has passed. The characters and circumstances are fictional; the learner must judge the specific evidence rather than assign a personality label.

turns.speaker: Ellie
turns.text: I meant to watch one clip but it kept suggesting another.

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Did you choose each next video?

turns.speaker: Ellie
turns.text: No. It automatically played and I kept scrolling.

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: What would make stopping a deliberate choice?

misinformation.title: Three articles that actually share one source
misinformation.intro: A claim is circulating that a research centre secretly changed its results. The characters and circumstances are fictional; the learner must judge the specific evidence rather than assign a personality label.

turns.speaker: Ari
turns.text: I found three sites making the same allegation.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Do they cite different documents?

turns.speaker: Ari
turns.text: All three quote a single anonymous post.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Then we have repetition, not three independent confirmations.

neurodiversity.title: A missed transition interpreted as unwillingness
neurodiversity.intro: A staff member with ADHD struggles when a meeting is moved with no notice. The characters and circumstances are fictional; the learner must judge the specific evidence rather than assign a personality label.

turns.speaker: Kai
turns.text: I had set reminders for tomorrow, not today.

turns.speaker: Manager
turns.text: Everyone else adjusted; you did not care enough.

turns.speaker: Kai
turns.text: I can attend if schedule changes are put in the calendar when decided.

turns.speaker: Manager
turns.text: I thought the group message was enough.

sleep.title: Sleep effort and clock checking
sleep.intro: A person lying awake checks the clock repeatedly and predicts the next day will be ruined. The characters and circumstances are fictional; the learner must judge the specific evidence rather than assign a personality label.

turns.speaker: Lee
turns.text: It is 2:20. Now I only have five hours left.

turns.speaker: Pat
turns.text: Does watching the clock help you sleep?

turns.speaker: Lee
turns.text: No. It makes me calculate every minute I am failing.

turns.speaker: Pat
turns.text: Could the clock be part of the cycle?

low-mood.title: Waiting for motivation before reconnecting
low-mood.intro: A person misses a weekly community activity that once mattered to them. The characters and circumstances are fictional; the learner must judge the specific evidence rather than assign a personality label.

turns.speaker: Sol
turns.text: I cannot go until I feel like myself again.

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Would a shorter visit be possible, or would it cost too much right now?

turns.speaker: Sol
turns.text: Maybe thirty minutes. A whole afternoon feels impossible.

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Could that be a useful test rather than a promise to feel cheerful?

scams.title: A believable bank caller and a new payment destination
scams.intro: A caller says a savings account is under attack and asks for an immediate protective transfer. The characters and circumstances are fictional; the learner must judge the specific evidence rather than assign a personality label.

turns.speaker: Caller
turns.text: We are from fraud prevention. Move your funds now to the secure account.

turns.speaker: Mina
turns.text: Can I hang up and call the number on my bank card?

turns.speaker: Caller
turns.text: Do not. The line may be compromised; you have only five minutes.

turns.speaker: Mina
turns.text: I will verify independently before doing anything.

masculinity.title: A gender expectation replaces a preference discussion
masculinity.intro: A couple disagree about a partner wearing makeup for a social event. The characters and circumstances are fictional; the learner must judge the specific evidence rather than assign a personality label.

turns.speaker: Eli
turns.text: I would like to try subtle makeup at the event.

turns.speaker: Morgan
turns.text: Men should not wear makeup. It embarrasses me.

turns.speaker: Eli
turns.text: You can dislike the look, but I want to choose my own presentation.

turns.speaker: Morgan
turns.text: I thought our relationship had traditional roles.

vaping.title: A social cue that turns into a dependence loop
vaping.intro: An apprentice vapes during breaks and now feels irritable before each break. The characters and circumstances are fictional; the learner must judge the specific evidence rather than assign a personality label.

turns.speaker: Rae
turns.text: I used to vape only when the others did.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: What happens now if you skip a break?

turns.speaker: Rae
turns.text: I feel restless and think I need it to concentrate.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Could some of that relief be from withdrawal?

conversation-patterns.title: One statement, two plausible interpretations
conversation-patterns.intro: A person requests a ten-minute pause during an argument and the other calls it a silent treatment. The characters and circumstances are fictional; the learner must judge the specific evidence rather than assign a personality label.

turns.speaker: Jules
turns.text: I am overwhelmed. Can we talk at eight when I can focus?

turns.speaker: Pia
turns.text: You are punishing me by refusing to speak.

turns.speaker: Jules
turns.text: I will come back at eight. I am not asking you to change your mind.

turns.speaker: Pia
turns.text: I thought any break meant you were withdrawing love.
